content.value_statement: Inconsistent commit messages make project history difficult to scan and automate. This skill analyzes Git changes and proposes project-specific Conventional Commit messages.
actual_capabilities: Analyze staged and unstaged Git changes using status and diff commands.
Select Conventional Commit types and project-specific scopes from changed files.
Generate concise subjects, optional bodies, issue footers, and breaking change notices.
Validate wording, length, type, scope, and punctuation against documented rules.
Explain type and scope choices and offer alternative commit messages.
Format copy-ready single-line and multiline Git commit commands.
limitations: Project-specific scopes target Logseq Template Graph and may not fit other repositories.
Git repository and shell access are required to inspect current changes.
The skill does not stage files or guarantee that a commit captures the intended work.
Issue references and breaking changes require evidence in the diff or user context.

use_cases.title: Prepare a focused feature commit
use_cases.description: Review staged changes and produce a concise message with the correct project scope.

use_cases.title: Review commit message quality
use_cases.description: Check type, scope, wording, length, and punctuation before accepting a contribution.

use_cases.title: Document a breaking release change
use_cases.description: Create a breaking-change commit with rationale, migration guidance, and issue references.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest a staged commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one Conventional Commit message. Explain the selected type and scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an existing message
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this commit message against project rules: {message}. Identify problems and provide a corrected version.

prompt_templates.title: Separate unrelated changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze staged and unstaged changes, separate unrelated work, and propose one commit message for each logical change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a mixed working tree.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a breaking change
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the staged diff for breaking changes. Produce a commit with body, migration guidance, issue footer, and a safe shell command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release preparation with migration impact.

output_examples.input: I added a Recipe class and cooking properties to the creative-work module.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(classes): add Recipe class with cooking properties. The classes scope reflects the primary change.

output_examples.input: The spouse property now supports multiple values instead of one.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: fix(properties): correct spouse property cardinality to many. A short body can explain the data-model correction.

output_examples.input: I removed the deprecated Customer class and added a replacement property.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(classes)!: remove deprecated Customer class. Add a breaking-change footer with migration steps.

best_practices: Stage one logical change before requesting a commit message.
Provide issue numbers and migration details when they are not visible in the diff.
Review every generated shell command and commit message before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague subjects such as update files or fix bug.
Do not combine unrelated changes under one broad commit message.
Do not claim issue references, performance gains, or breaking impact without evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill create the commit automatically?
faq.answer: It proposes messages and commands. Execution depends on tool permissions and user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it inspect unstaged changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect staged and unstaged diffs, but commit suggestions prioritize staged work.

faq.question: Does it work outside Logseq Template Graph?
faq.answer: The general format transfers, but project-specific scopes and file mappings may require adjustment.

faq.question: How are breaking changes handled?
faq.answer: The skill adds the breaking marker, footer, rationale, and migration guidance when evidence supports them.

faq.question: Can it add issue references?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide issue or pull request numbers when they are not visible in repository context.

faq.question: Which shell format does it use?
faq.answer: Examples use Bash and quoted heredocs for multiline messages. Review and adapt commands for your shell.
